name: gov.sg SMS Sender ID (OGP/GovTech)

scam_info.sample: This is a full list of the SMS Sender IDs that are not combined under the gov.sg Sender ID, and will continue to be used separately. ... 72255 Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) Two-way communications for National Service matters
scam_info.notes: Authoritative allowlist of the 8 government sender IDs that are not gov.sg: 72255 (MINDEF, NS two-way), 70999 (MHA/Police emergency SMS), 70995 (MHA/SCDF 995 SMS), MHAalert (MHA public alerts), 80709999 (SPF NS mobilisation; previously 83385761), 80709995 (SCDF NS call-ups; previously 91449746), "POLICE 999" (SPF emergency video link / silent-call advisory), "SCDF 995" (SCDF emergency video link). "Updated 12 Sep 2024".

Searchable list of agencies that do or do not send from gov.sg. The data is inlined in the page's static Next.js bundle (/_next/static/chunks/app/check/page-*.js), with no API call: 206 organisations, 128 sending from gov.sg, 78 not (schools, IHLs, public hospitals, etc.), and 3 with exceptions (MHA, SCDF, SPF). Bundle filename is content-hashed, so re-derive it from the /check HTML.

scam_info.sample: A gov.sg SMS will have all 4 of these indicators. If even one of them is missing, or you suspect an SMS may not be authentic, please report it immediately using this form .
scam_info.notes: The 4 authenticity cues are: lowercase "gov.sg" sender, message starts with the agency name, a fixed do-not-reply signature, and a single threaded conversation. Suspicious SMS reports go to go.gov.sg/report-sms. Blog (/blog) has 3 posts (Jan-Mar 2025). robots: allow all; no sitemap (/sitemap.xml 404).

notes: Built by Open Government Products (GovTech) per the site footer. Best machine-usable SMS allowlist in the partition (sender IDs + org list).
